choices.text: Find a home in the hills.

c5_champion.title: The Champion at the Bridge

choices.text: Cross the bridge. Meet him in single combat.
Send Theodore. The undying cannot be killed.

c5_champ_hit.title: A Sword Through the Dead
c5_champ_hit.text: {{knows_varric|You have waited for this. Varric's sword is quick, but your hatred is quicker. He falls on the bridge boards, and his helm rolls into the river. The dead are silent. You have taken their lord.}}{{!knows_varric|The champion falls, and the host sags. For a moment you can feel their purpose waver.}}

c5_champ_mixed.title: A Hard-Won Blow
c5_champ_mixed.text: You lose a hand's width of skin from your forearm, but the champion falls. The host recoils.

c5_champ_miss.title: Beaten Back
c5_champ_miss.text: The champion's sword goes through your shoulder before Roland drags you away. You live. Hartmann holds the bridge until the wound can be bound.

c5_bridge_hold.title: Hold the Bridge
c5_bridge_hold.text:
You do not have the Skull armed, and you do not have the fire-rafts ready, but you have a stone bridge, a chain, and a line of pikes.

The dead come across in files of six. Roland and Corbin hold the right. Hartmann holds the left. You hold the centre.

c5_hold_hit.title: The Bridge Holds
c5_hold_hit.text: By dawn the bridge is a drift of broken things, and you are still standing. The host withdraws, bleeding, and the Bell on the mountain tolls the last of them down.

c5_hold_mixed.title: Barely
c5_hold_mixed.text: You hold it, barely. Three of the pikemen are dead, and Corbin has lost two fingers. But the dawn comes.

c5_hold_miss.title: The Line Breaks
c5_hold_miss.text: The right flank gives at midnight. You fall back across the bridge into the lock-house with a dozen survivors, and slam the door.

c6_found.title: Founding
c6_found.text:
The mountain above the abbey has a long shelf of rock, a spring, and a view down three valleys. It is the best place you have seen in a year, and it is nothing yet. A kingdom needs more than a standard, and you have the people to build it.

Durgan paces the ground with a measuring-cord, grumbling about foundations. Isobel stands with the ledger.

"We have the labour for three works before winter," she says. "Choose well."

choices.text: The Mill — a water-wheel on the spring, to grind grain and drive saws.
The Granary — stone-vaulted, rat-proof, big enough for a winter.
The Chapel — a place for Anselm and Ambrose to hold the dead's rites.
The Wall — a curtain of dwarf-cut stone around the shelf.
The Bell-Mount — a tower to carry the Bell and the Skull.
The Sky-Farms — terraced fields cut into the cliff.

c6_year.title: A Year
c6_year.text:
A winter passes. Then a spring. Then a harvest.

The works go up. The Wall rises, or doesn't. The grain comes in, or doesn't. Your people stop looking over their shoulders at every sound, and begin, cautiously, to look at each other.

By the next autumn there are children playing in the courtyard.

{{queen_saoirse|By the autumn after that, a baby is born in the royal chambers: a frail, red-haired, green-eyed boy who does not cry as loud as he should.}}{{!queen_saoirse|You sit at the high table, and look at the empty chair beside you, and think about lines that end.}}

c6_heir.title: The Heir
c6_heir.text:
He is light as a loaf. His breathing is a small, steady rasp. Ambrose says what he can: sun, care, patience. Ferrand says the same, more carefully.

Saoirse watches you hold your son with something unreadable in her face.

"He will live," she says, "because I have decided it."

You are not at all sure that it is up to her.

c6_feast.title: The Feast of the First Harvest
c6_feast.text:
A great table runs the length of the courtyard. Dwarf-brewed ale, fen-smoked eel, orchard apples from Ashgrove. The Red Hand brothers sing hymns with their shirts undone. Halbrecht, who still doesn't call you Majesty, stands to toast "the man who didn't die."

It is the first night in two years that no one keeps watch from the wall.

At the end of the table, Lady Isobel sits straight as a rod, glaring at Durgan, who is trying very hard not to look at her.

choices.text: Play the matchmaker. Pair the widows of the column with the bachelor dwarves.
Let them find their own way. Enjoy the night.

c6_match_hit.title: Marriages
c6_match_hit.text:
By the end of the night there are six pairs at the table, and one pair, Lady Isobel and Durgan the Stone-Warden, that has stopped pretending not to be. She marries him the next spring, in the Chapel, with a dwarven crown-of-iron in her hair.

A generation of children will be born of this table: half-height, strong-willed, and, you suspect, impossible.

c6_match_mixed.title: A Few Matches
c6_match_mixed.text: Some pairs take. Some do not. Isobel, however, stands up from her chair and informs Durgan, in front of everyone, that if he is going to stare at her he may as well ask. He does.

c6_match_miss.title: Awkward
c6_match_miss.text: It is a disaster. Three widows storm off. A dwarf proposes to a goat. Isobel looks at you with a flat, tired expression that says: *this is exactly why I hate you.*

c6_levy.title: The Levy
c6_levy.text:
In the spring the scouts return with the same report: the dead are massing again in the lowlands. Malgareth is not a lich who forgets.

Aldric, now sixteen, is the obvious choice for Captain of the Levy. He is stiff with pride and terrified in the right ways.

"How many men do I need?"

choices.text: "All of them. Every adult with legs."
"Eight hundred. The best. The rest hold the wall."

c6_levy_all.title: Everyone
c6_levy_all.text:
Aldric nods, pale. "Everyone, then."

By midsummer there are two thousand people under arms and no one in the fields. It is the kind of army that wins by exhausting itself on the enemy.

choices.text: Send Sam to the fen for reinforcements.

c6_levy_elite.title: Eight Hundred
c6_levy_elite.text: Eight hundred men trained by dwarf and Red Hand, led by a sixteen-year-old with his father's sword. They are not a horde. They are a blade.

choices.text: Send Sam to the fen for reinforcements.

c6_sam.title: The Squire's Errand
c6_sam.text:
Sam is twenty now, no longer a boy, and still serves as your squire out of pure stubbornness. You hand him a letter, a seal, and a fen-boat.

"Go to the Fenmarch. Bring me the warriors the queen has promised."

He grins. "And if she's in a mood?"

"Bring your charm."

choices.text: A scout rides in. The Abbot wants to see you. At once.

c6_season.title: The Turning Year
c6_season.text: The seasons turn on the mountain. Wood-smoke and snow. Mud. Bees in the kitchen-garden. Every few weeks, something new asks for your attention.

c6_ev_famine_r0.title: A Lean Winter
c6_ev_famine_r0.text: The reserve carries you through. By spring the stores are empty and the people are alive.

c6_ev_famine_r1.title: A Lean Winter
c6_ev_famine_r1.text: Isobel's rationing is merciless and exact. No one starves. A few people hate her for it. She is entirely unrepentant.

c6_ev_famine_r2.title: A Lean Winter
c6_ev_famine_r2.text: Half the party returns. They bring venison, deer-hides and a grim reluctance to speak of what they saw.

c6_ev_famine_r3.title: A Lean Winter
c6_ev_famine_r3.text: The stew-ponds, thank God, were stocked. By spring you will never eat fish again.

c6_ev_famine.title: A Lean Winter
c6_ev_famine.text: The snow comes early and stays late. By midwinter the granary is two-thirds empty, and the children have learned to play at being hungry.

choices.text: Open the sealed stores. Spend the reserve.
Trust Isobel's ledger. She has been right so far.
Send hunting parties to the lowlands, past the dead.
Eat the carp. All of it.

c6_ev_plague_r0.title: The Cough
c6_ev_plague_r0.text: It costs a week, and eleven lives, but the cough burns out.

c6_ev_plague_r1.title: The Cough
c6_ev_plague_r1.text: Brom's tonic is vile and works. The cough fades, and Brom drinks the leftovers himself, 'to be safe'.

c6_ev_plague_r2.title: The Cough
c6_ev_plague_r2.text: Ambrose and his three hundred chant for nine days. Whether it was the prayers or the weather, the cough lifts.

c6_ev_plague.title: The Cough
c6_ev_plague.text: A wasting cough runs through the lower huts. Brom suspects the water. Ferrand, if he were alive, would suspect something worse.

choices.text: Boil all water; quarantine the sick in the old chapel.
Ask Brom to brew a deep-cap tonic.

c6_ev_brawl_r0.title: Dwarf and Man
c6_ev_brawl_r0.text: You end up with a black eye and two grudging apologies.

c6_ev_brawl_r1.title: Dwarf and Man
c6_ev_brawl_r1.text: Bruni and Vance share a bench for a week, glaring and drinking. It does more for unity than your whole speech.

c6_ev_brawl_r2.title: Dwarf and Man
c6_ev_brawl_r2.text: The brawl ends instantly. So does something else.

c6_ev_brawl.title: Dwarf and Man
c6_ev_brawl.text: A tavern argument escalates. A dwarf and a Red Hand brother, a dispute over a seat, and then a table. By evening it is thirty men, and someone has drawn a knife.

choices.text: Stand between them. Make them break it up.
Have Bruni and Vance sort it. They respect each other.
Hang the first man to draw steel.

c6_ev_emissary_r0.title: A Grey Emissary
c6_ev_emissary_r0.text: The rider crumbles. The scroll curls. Malgareth's invitation goes unanswered.

c6_ev_emissary_r1.title: A Grey Emissary
c6_ev_emissary_r1.text: The mountain listens. The mountain laughs. The rider rides home with a hundred insults. It is the best morale you've had in months.

c6_ev_emissary_r2.title: A Grey Emissary
c6_ev_emissary_r2.text: Alcuin's reply is a masterpiece of deception. The lich will believe whatever he is told for a month.

c6_ev_emissary_r3.title: A Grey Emissary
c6_ev_emissary_r3.text: He names a price. It is a good price. You tell yourself you are only listening.

c6_ev_emissary.title: A Grey Emissary
c6_ev_emissary.text:
A skeletal rider approaches the mountain gate under a white flag. It carries a scroll, written in a hand you recognise: the lich's own.

The scroll is an invitation to treat. It says Malgareth will pay for the Skull in any coin you name.

choices.text: Burn the scroll. Burn the rider.
Read it aloud to the whole mountain. Let them hear the offer.
Send an answer through Alcuin's channel.
Entertain the offer. Ask for terms.

c6_ev_caravan_r0.title: Caravan from the Lowlands
c6_ev_caravan_r0.text: The mountain smells of salt for a month. The smiths hammer all night.

c6_ev_caravan_r1.title: Caravan from the Lowlands
c6_ev_caravan_r1.text: The merchants pay, sullenly. They do not come back.

c6_ev_caravan_r2.title: Caravan from the Lowlands
c6_ev_caravan_r2.text: Half the caravan stays. By autumn there is a market street. Bael weeps with joy.

c6_ev_caravan.title: Caravan from the Lowlands
c6_ev_caravan.text: A caravan of eight wagons toils up the mountain road, led by a woman who claims to be Bael's cousin. They are carrying cloth, nails, salt, and a rumour that the dead are thinning in the southern vales.

choices.text: Trade fairly. Buy salt and nails.
Tax them. A king is owed his due.
Offer them a place. A market, a street, a guildhall.

c6_ev_wedding_r0.title: A Wedding in the Chapel
c6_ev_wedding_r0.text: It is the shortest speech you have ever made and the one most remembered.

c6_ev_wedding_r1.title: A Wedding in the Chapel
c6_ev_wedding_r1.text: It is a disaster. It is also the best night of the year.

c6_ev_wedding_r2.title: A Wedding in the Chapel
c6_ev_wedding_r2.text: The room erupts. Saoirse's eyebrow rises, then her smile.

c6_ev_wedding.title: A Wedding in the Chapel
c6_ev_wedding.text:
Two of the column marry in the new chapel: a Red Hand brother and a widow from Tollmere. Ambrose officiates. The dwarves bring a barrel of something terrible.

You are asked to give a toast.

choices.text: Give a long, rambling toast. Let the wine speak.
Announce your own betrothal to the Fen-Queen.

c6_ev_rockfall_r0.title: Rockfall
c6_ev_rockfall_r0.text: You dig for six hours. The masons live. You do not feel your hands for a day.

c6_ev_rockfall_r1.title: Rockfall
c6_ev_rockfall_r1.text: Durgan arrives with a hammer and a profane vocabulary. In an hour the rubble is a road.

c6_ev_rockfall_r2.title: Rockfall
c6_ev_rockfall_r2.text: Three dwarf masons die. Every dwarf on the mountain remembers.

c6_ev_rockfall.title: Rockfall
c6_ev_rockfall.text: After a winter thaw, the east face of the new Wall slumps. Boulders block the road, and three dwarf masons are trapped under a collapsed scaffold.

choices.text: Dig them out yourself, with the labour gang.
Let the masons go. The Wall matters more.

c6_ev_bandits_r0.title: Lowland Bandits
c6_ev_bandits_r0.text: Corbin brings back eleven heads, three prisoners, and a very poor mood.

c6_ev_bandits_r1.title: Lowland Bandits
c6_ev_bandits_r1.text: Twenty-two accept. Eight vanish in the night. The rest become good farmers.

c6_ev_bandits_r2.title: Lowland Bandits
c6_ev_bandits_r2.text: It's a hard week. Roland takes an arrow in the shoulder. The bandits are no more.

c6_ev_bandits.title: Lowland Bandits
c6_ev_bandits.text: A band of thirty men, the remains of some defeated lord's levy, has taken the lower road and is robbing pilgrims.

choices.text: Offer them land and pardon. Recruit them.
Hunt them down yourself with the knights.

c6_ev_omen_r0.title: Anselm's Vision
c6_ev_omen_r0.text: He does not know. He says only: the thing is waiting, and has been waiting a very long time, and is *patient.*

c6_ev_omen_r1.title: Anselm's Vision
c6_ev_omen_r1.text: He nods, shaky, and leaves. You do not sleep.

c6_ev_omen_r2.title: Anselm's Vision
c6_ev_omen_r2.text: The dead man's eye opens, wet and white, and for a long moment it looks at the Skull. Then it closes. Something in the mountain exhales.

c6_ev_omen.title: Anselm's Vision
c6_ev_omen.text:
Anselm comes to your door at midnight, white-faced, hands trembling.

"The Skull spoke," he says. "Not in words. I saw a throne of coins, and a thing on it, and a door. I saw you, and I saw the door open."

choices.text: Press him: what did he see behind the door?
Calm him. Visions are not orders.
Take the Skull to Ferrand's crypt. See what the eye does.

c6_ev_fen_r0.title: A Fen Delegation
c6_ev_fen_r0.text: The fen-folk are astonished and delighted. A treaty is signed that evening.

c6_ev_fen_r1.title: A Fen Delegation
c6_ev_fen_r1.text: They have two hundred, and send half. The rest will come at harvest.

c6_ev_fen_r2.title: A Fen Delegation
c6_ev_fen_r2.text: The elders bow so low their cloaks sweep the dust.

c6_ev_fen_r3.title: A Fen Delegation
c6_ev_fen_r3.text: They leave in silence. You have the unpleasant feeling you made a mistake.

c6_ev_fen.title: A Fen Delegation
c6_ev_fen.text: Six reed-boats arrive at the mountain's foot with a delegation from the Fenmarch: elders in woven cloaks, a choir of children, a ceremonial eel.

choices.text: Receive them in the Great Hall with full honours.
Ask for their warriors, as promised.
Send them away empty-handed: the mountain has nothing to give.

c6_ev_pilgrims_r0.title: Pilgrims
c6_ev_pilgrims_r0.text: They weep. They stay. The Chapel will need a second altar.

c6_ev_pilgrims_r1.title: Pilgrims
c6_ev_pilgrims_r1.text: Anselm blesses them instead, with a quiet look at you.

c6_ev_pilgrims_r2.title: Pilgrims
c6_ev_pilgrims_r2.text: Thirty of them take the oath. They will die for it, gladly.

c6_ev_pilgrims.title: Pilgrims
c6_ev_pilgrims.text:
They come up the mountain road on foot, a hundred strong: the last faithful of Saint Gregory's pilgrim-orders, drawn by the rumour of a king who carries the Skull.

They kneel in the snow, and refuse to rise until you bless them.

choices.text: Bless them as a king and a pilgrim.
Recruit the strongest as the Skull's honour-guard.

c6_heir_choice.title: The Child's Breath
c6_heir_choice.text:
The boy's breathing worsens through the winter. Ferrand, if he lived, would counsel patience. Ambrose counsels sun and rest. Saoirse counsels nothing at all; she simply sits by the cradle with her hand on his small chest, night after night.

Anselm, softly, at your elbow: "The Skull has healed before. At a cost."

choices.text: Ask Anselm to hold the Skull over the child.
Take the boy to the sun-farms each dawn, and pray to the saint yourself.

c6_heir_skull.title: The Skull's Gift
c6_heir_skull.text:
Anselm lays the Skull on the boy's chest. It does nothing, for a long breath. Then the child coughs, wetly, and cries — a loud, furious, living wail.

Saoirse laughs and weeps together. You hold your son and cannot speak.

But Anselm, kneeling, looks at the Skull, and then at you. "It is a little less than it was," he says. "A little. I am not sure what it cost."

c6_heir_wait.title: Patience
c6_heir_wait.text:
You take the boy to the sun each morning. You warm his tiny feet. You sing him the lullabies your own nurse sang. By spring, he is thin but breathing, and by summer he has begun to grab at your beard.

He will be a quiet child, a watchful one. But he will live.

c6_heir_pray.title: A King's Vigil
c6_heir_pray.text:
For forty mornings you carry the boy up to the cliff-farms and hold him in the first light. You say the saint's prayer over him until the words lose meaning. Somewhere in the fortieth, you notice he is smiling.

It might be the sun. It might be the saint. It might simply be a father's stubbornness.

c6_adopt.title: An Heir Without a Queen
c6_adopt.text:
You have no wife and no child. The line of Gregory ends with you, unless you do something about it.

{{emmet_adopted|Emmet, the boy from the road, has taken to following you with his wooden horse.}}{{tom_saved|Tom, the one-legged boy you held at Aldermont, has grown into a solemn youth, and looks at you with an expression you recognise.}}

choices.text: Adopt Emmet, the lost boy of the Weald.
Take Tom as your ward. He has earned it.
Name young Aldric your heir. He is young enough to learn.
Name no one. A king need not choose today.

c7_library.title: The Concordance
c7_library.text:
Ambrose has not slept. He has the Concordance open across three tables, with notes in his own hand weighted down by a candlestick.

"I will tell you what I know," he says, "and then you will not like it."

The thing beneath the Deepholt is a necromancer of the First Era: a servant of the Enemy, one of seven, who calls itself a god and hoards what it takes. Everything the dwarves lost, it kept — gold, banners, bones. It has been feeding on the drowned dead of six sealed levels for a thousand years. Malgareth is its steward, not its master.

"Kill the god," says Ambrose, "and the horde above falls with it. That is what the Concordance says. I do not know if it is true."

He lowers his voice. "There is a name. I will write it, and seal it, and give it to you at the door. Not before."

{{ferrand_dead|In the crypt below the chapel, Brother Ferrand's body lies on its slab, where he died of the bite last winter. Anselm says the dead man's left eye has begun to open when the Skull passes. No one has found the courage to say what that means.}}

choices.text: Gather the Court. Decide how to go down.

c7_decide.title: Above and Below
c7_decide.text:
The scouts say fifteen thousand dead are on the road, led by Malgareth's second host. The Wall and the Bell can hold them for a time. But a time is all you have.

The descent will take days. Food below is finite. The walls above are finite. Two clocks, running at once.

And the Skull can only be in one place.

choices.text: Take the Skull below. It makes the dead stop. The delve will go quicker, safer. The Bell rings plain above.
Leave the Skull in the Bell. Let it hold the wall, and go down without it.

c7_party.title: The Descent Party
c7_party.text:
Who goes?

Roland, to carry the standard. Durgan, who knows the stairs. Anselm, to hold the Skull. Theodore, who cannot be killed. Hetta, to scout.

Everyone else holds the mountain: Aldric on the wall, Isobel at the ledgers, Ambrose at the Bell. You look at them all, and the whole kingdom looks back at you.

choices.text: Open the door to the Deepholt. Descend.

c7_l1.title: Level One: The Wet Stair
c7_l1.text:
The First Hall is quiet. The doors to the stair stand open, and below them a great flight of steps drops into black water.

Durgan lowers his lantern. "Flooded since the first time we sealed it. The water is the lich's, not ours."

Things move in it. They aren't breathing, but they are listening.

choices.text: Have Durgan cut a dry path along the wall. It will take a day.
Anselm lifts the Skull. The drowned stop.
Hold up the delvers' lantern: the water-things shrink from its light.
Descend by rope-shaft, bypassing the stair.

c7_l1_ok.title: Down the Stair
c7_l1_ok.text: You reach the landing wet and cold and whole. Behind you the water closes like a held breath.

c7_l1_cost.title: A Soaked Pack
c7_l1_cost.text: The supplies are spoiled by the water. You reach the landing but the packs are heavy and sour.

c7_l1_bad.title: Hands in the Water
c7_l1_bad.text: Something takes your ankle and pulls. By the time Roland hauls you free, you've swallowed half the stair, and the packs have gone under.

c7_l2.title: Level Two: The Hoard
c7_l2.text:
A vault the size of a cathedral, filled to the rafters with treasure: heaped coin, gem-studded armour, ranks of gold idols, dwarven banners worked in silver thread. Everything the Deepholt lost, kept in mounds.

Durgan stops walking. His hand is on his hammer, and the knuckles are white.

"My grandfather's crown," he says quietly. "There. On the pile."

The coin murmurs. It is not a sound. It is the *impression* of a sound, as of something that wants.

choices.text: Touch nothing. Walk the path through the middle.
Take the crown for Durgan. A king gives gifts.
Scoop the treasure. The realm needs gold. (+200 coin.)

c7_l2_purse.title: A Little Weight
c7_l2_purse.text:
You take only what fits in a pocket. The coins are cold. For a moment you could swear one of them *whispered*.

Roland says nothing. Durgan says nothing. The silence is very loud.

c7_l2_crown.title: The Crown of Durgan's Grandfather
c7_l2_crown.text:
You lift it down. The hoard sighs. The stone floor trembles, then settles. Durgan takes the crown with both hands and weeps openly.

"I have waited three hundred years to hold this."

It will matter later. Durgan does not forget a gift.

c7_l2_loot.title: A King's Ransom
c7_l2_loot.text:
You load a canvas sack with a stranger's life's work. It is the most you have held since the Ford. The hoard does not seem to mind.

Yet.

c7_l2_wights.title: Hoard-Wights
c7_l2_wights.text:
The coins stand up. Not literally, though they might as well: the pile coughs up a dozen things in dead-gold armour, hollow-eyed, bearing the shapes of dwarves long buried.

They come for you.

choices.text: Fight them with Roland and Theodore.
Anselm lifts the Skull. They stop.

c7_l3.title: Level Three: The Drowned Barracks

choices.text: Cross the hall in silence. Do not wake them.
Anselm lifts the Skull. Walk through them.
Theodore walks ahead. The undying knight cannot be harmed by them.
Hetta scouts a safe path among the bunks.

c7_l3_ok.title: Past the Sleepers
c7_l3_ok.text:
You cross the hall. The dead do not stir. At the pillar the chained man raises his head, and the lamp reveals his face.

{{bors_taken|It is Bors.}}

c7_l3_theo.title: The Undying Walks First
c7_l3_theo.text:
Theodore walks down the aisle between the bunks, hand on his sword. The sleepers turn their heads to follow him and do not rise. The undying knight reaches the pillar first and cuts the chain.

"I know this face," he says. "He rode with me."

c7_l3_wake.title: They Wake
c7_l3_wake.text: A bunk creaks. Then another. Then six hundred wet hands push against stone, and the whole hall sits up together.

choices.text: Run for the pillar. Cut the prisoner free and go.

c7_l3_free.title: The Prisoner
c7_l3_free.text:
{{bors_taken|"Sire," says Bors, with a voice like a rusted hinge. "I held out as long as I could. Not very long."}}{{!bors_taken|The man is Sir Garrick of the old garrison — one of the Deepholt's human wardens. "Six years," he says. "I thought it was six years."}}

He is thin, bearded, and alive. That is more than you expected.

choices.text: Share your rations. Bring him with you.
Send him up with Hetta. He is too weak to follow.

c7_l4.title: Level Four: The Sunless Market
c7_l4.text:
A great square of stone shopfronts, long vacated, lit by a cold, steady green glow. Stalls hold bone-carved wares, books of grey skin, dolls with too many joints.

In the centre of the square, seated on a plain stool, the grey-robed lich Malgareth is waiting.

"King Gregory," he says gently. "Sit. We have so little time, and so much to say."

choices.text: Refuse to sit. Stand and speak.
The old map shows a ladder behind the third pillar. Skip the Market.

c7_malgareth.title: A Lich's Offer
c7_malgareth.text:
He has a quiet, scholarly manner. "The god below is not my master. It is my jailer. It took me at the Ford of an older river, three hundred years ago, and I have served ever since. I do not enjoy it."

He lifts one gloved hand. "Give me the Skull. I will use it to put it down. I have studied the Skull for three centuries. You have carried it for three weeks. Which of us is better qualified?"

It is the most reasonable offer you have heard in two years.

choices.text: "No. I will not hand the Skull to you."
"Tell me how to kill it. Tell me the weakness."

c7_malg_no.title: A Disappointed Scholar
c7_malg_no.text:
"A pity," says Malgareth. He gets to his feet, brushing dust from his robes. "I do not have the strength to take it from you. I had hoped you would be persuadable."

He steps aside. "The stair is that way. I shall wait here. Perhaps we will speak again."

c7_malg_weakness.title: The Truth, For Once
c7_malg_weakness.text:
Malgareth hesitates for a long moment. The green light flickers.

"It is bound to its hoard. Every coin is a nail in its coffin. If the hoard is scattered, it weakens. If the Skull is raised in its throne-room, it *stops*."

He looks almost relieved. "I have never told anyone that. It took me three centuries to find the courage."

c7_malg_half.title: A Half-Truth
c7_malg_half.text:
"The Skull is a part of it," he says carefully. "And the hoard is a part. But I do not know all the parts."

It is not nothing.

c7_malg_lie.title: A Lie
c7_malg_lie.text: He smiles his small, old smile. "Strike it in the heart," says Malgareth, and says nothing more. You are not certain he told you the truth.

c7_malg_deal.title: The Skull Changes Hands
c7_malg_deal.text:
You hold out the box. Malgareth takes it with both hands, as one takes a newborn. He lifts the lid.

The Skull lies in its cloth. Malgareth looks at it for a very long time.

Then he closes the lid and hands it back.

"You would have given it to me," he says wonderingly. "I did not think anyone would."

He steps aside. "Go down. I will not follow. I am tired of following."

c7_malg_stand.title: Words Standing Up
c7_malg_stand.text:
You do not sit. Malgareth lifts one eyebrow, amused, and lets the silence drag.

"As you wish," he says. "The question stands."

c7_malg_fight.title: Steel on Bone
c7_malg_fight.text: Roland and Theodore charge. Malgareth is no swordsman, but he does not need to be: the green light flares, and the stalls of the Market begin to stand up, shelf by shelf, and come for you.

c7_malg_win.title: The Steward Falls Back
c7_malg_win.text:
The lich staggers, gutted by Roland's blade, and vanishes into the green dark with a hiss.

He will not die. But he is wounded, and the road to the fifth level is open.

c7_malg_drive.title: Overrun
c7_malg_drive.text: The Market overwhelms you. Theodore holds the stair so the rest of you can retreat. It is an expensive retreat.

c7_malg_skull.title: Stopped
c7_malg_skull.text:
Anselm lifts the Skull. The stalls fall back into silence. Malgareth stares at it from across the square, and something in his face breaks.

"Take it away," he says in a very small voice. "*Please.*"

He retreats into the dark.

c7_l5.title: Level Five: The Cistern of Names
c7_l5.text:
A round hall, a great black cistern in the centre, lined with the names of the dead. Thousands. Each carved in a different hand.

Anselm kneels at the edge of the water and reads, his lips moving.

"They're all here," he says. "Every soul it took. It keeps them."

The water begins to ripple, as though something very large has noticed you.

choices.text: Read the names aloud. Give them back their dead.
Cross quickly. There is no time for grief.
Break the cistern. Let the names go.

c7_l5_read.title: The Reading of the Names
c7_l5_read.text:
It takes an hour. Anselm reads. Alcuin, who is not even here — you realise it is Roland reading, in a voice you have never heard from him.

When you are finished the water is still. Something in the black has turned, and let go.

choices.text: Go on to the last stair.

c7_l5_break.title: Durgan's Hammer
c7_l5_break.text:
Durgan brings his hammer down once, twice, three times on the lip of the cistern. The stone cracks. The water drains away into the rock with a sound like a long exhale.

"There," he says. "Let them rest."

choices.text: Go on to the last stair.

c7_l6.title: Level Six: The Door
c7_l6.text:
The last stair ends at a door of black iron, the height of three men. Hinges the size of a bull. A single keyhole, no bigger than your thumb.

Ambrose's sealed letter is in your pocket, as he promised. You break the wax and read the name. You do not speak it. You do not need to.

From behind the door comes the grinding hum you first heard in the Great Hall: the sound of something enormous, thinking.

choices.text: Turn back. Seal the door again. You have done enough.

c7_throne.title: The Throne of the Hoarder
c7_throne.text:
It is not a throne-room. It is the heart of a mountain, hollowed and lined with gold. A single seat of fused coin and bone. And upon it, the thing that calls itself a god.

It is not shaped like a man. It is not shaped like anything. It is a column of the dead, standing, bound by sinew and coin into a form that watches you with four hundred eyes.

"King Gregory," it says, in every voice it has ever eaten. "You have brought my bones back to me."

It means the Skull.

choices.text: Anselm lifts the Skull. End it.
Charge it with your sword. Roland and Theodore at your side.
Use the scattered hoard: break the coin-throne and unbind it.
Listen. Hear what the god has to offer a king.
Anselm lifts the Skull. It is dimmer than it was.
Drive Durgan's rune-blade into the seam: the heart of the throne.
Hold out until the Bell above is rung. Roland knows the hour.
Sound Durgan's great horn. The dwarf-host will come.
You are not alone. Look to the stair.
The god's voice sounds, very faintly, like your own.

c7_final_skull.title: The Skull Raised
c7_final_skull.text:
Anselm lifts the Skull and the whole chamber goes still.

The god sees it. It knows what it is. It opens its four hundred mouths and screams, and the scream is the sound of every soul it ever kept, rising at once.

Then the god *stops*. Coin by coin, bone by bone, the thing on the throne comes apart, and what is left is a dry, grey drift, like ash.

c7_final_hoard.title: The Throne Broken
c7_final_hoard.text:
You see it all at once: the coin and bone and gold lashed into a body. You see where the seams are, and which nail holds the rest.

"Durgan," you say. "The third rank from the left. The great banner-pole."

The dwarf's hammer comes down like a falling star.

c7_final_fight.title: The Last Battle
c7_final_fight.text:
The god fights as a dozen men would: a hundred arms, a hundred swords. Roland takes a blow meant for you. Theodore, the undying, simply stands in the doorway and refuses to move.

You hack at the throne with a king's sword and a king's courage. It is not enough. It is never enough.

choices.text: Anselm lifts the Skull at the last moment.
Throw everything into one last charge.
Fall back. This was a mistake.
Hold the doorway while Roland carries the Skull out.
Hold the doorway while Roland carries the Skull out.

c7_final_bargain.title: The Hollow Crown
c7_final_bargain.text:
The god leans forward. "A king without a kingdom. A man with a skull he cannot use. I offer you what you wanted at the Ford: a crown that cannot be taken. A realm that will not die. A people who will never leave you."

Its voice is very gentle.

"Kneel."

end_triumph.title: The Kingdom Under the Mountain
end_triumph.text:
You climb for two days. At the top of the stair the sun is a white wound in the sky, and the dead are lying on the slope of the mountain like fallen wheat. Aldric is on the wall. He sees the standard and begins to weep.

The horde does not rise. Malgareth's host lies still across a hundred miles of road.

{{bors_saved|Bors rides at your side in the procession, thin and quiet, and keeps his sword drawn for a month.}}{{theodore_back|Theodore, the undying, takes the Wall. He does not sleep. He does not need to.}}{{isobel_durgan|Isobel and Durgan hold the Great Hall together, and the dwarves rebuild it in her name.}}{{heir_frail|Your son sees the sun for the first time on the day you return. He cries, loud for once, and Saoirse laughs until she weeps.}}{{durgan_crown|Durgan wears his grandfather's crown at the coronation, and swears a second time.}}

You do not sit on a throne. You sit on a stool by the fire in the Great Hall of the Deepholt, with a pipe in your mouth, and watch your people eat.

It is enough.
end_triumph.ending: TRIUMPH — The Kingdom Under the Mountain

end_sacrifice.title: The King Under the Mountain
end_sacrifice.text:
You send Roland up with the standard, and Anselm with the box. You stay, with Durgan, who refuses to leave, and Theodore, who cannot.

The door seals behind you. The three of you sit on the stone steps of a ruined throne-room and wait, as the god's ashes settle, in the dark.

Years later, the scholars say, a light is seen burning in the deepest window of the Deepholt. A king keeps watch.
end_sacrifice.ending: SACRIFICE — The King Under the Mountain

end_bargain.title: The Hollow Crown
end_bargain.text:
You kneel. The god puts its crown on your head: a ring of gold and bone and screaming faces.

For a thousand years you rule. Your Court never leaves you. Your people never die. They do not sleep, or eat, or leave. They simply stand in rows in the Great Hall of the Deepholt, eyes open, and obey.

Roland is the last to look at you with recognition. He kneels, too, and weeps, and does not rise.

end_flight.title: The Long Road
end_flight.text:
You seal the door behind you. Durgan sets the stone. Anselm says the old prayer. You climb.

The god below does not wake. Not that year. Not that decade. You and your people live in the mountain for a generation, and then, when you are old and the walls are strong, you wander back down to the lowlands and teach your grandchildren to listen at night for a sound beneath the floor.

You have not won. But you have not lost.

end_siege.title: The Walls Fall
end_siege.text:
You hear it first as a bell, ringing wild: Ambrose, shouting down the stair. Then the sound stops.

By the time you climb out, the mountain is burning. Isobel's ledger lies in the courtyard, pages scattered. Aldric's sword is in the stone beside the gate.

The dead have taken everything. You have the Skull. You have no one left to protect with it.

end_starve.title: The Dark Below
end_starve.text:
The food runs out on the fifth day. The lamps run out on the sixth. On the seventh, you sit in the dark with Roland, who says he is not hungry, and Theodore, who does not need to be.

Years later, someone finds your standard on the stair of the sixth level, folded neatly on a rock.

death.title: Gregory VII Falls
death.text:
You fall.

The last thing you see is Roland's face, white and furious, and the standard going down behind you like a flag in a storm.

There is no one to carry the Skull now. There is only the dark, and the voice of the god, patient, pleased.
death.ending: DEATH — Here Lies Gregory the Exiled

end_death.title: A Fatal Error
end_death.text: You fall back too late. The god's reach is long.

c7_r1a_r0.title: The Flooded Chapel
c7_r1a_r0.text: A cold peace. You rise lighter.

c7_r1a_r1.title: The Flooded Chapel
c7_r1a_r1.text: A reliquary, sealed. Inside, a thumb-bone of some dwarf-saint. Anselm reverently pockets it.

c7_r1a.title: The Flooded Chapel
c7_r1a.text: A chapel of the dwarf-saints, knee-deep in black water. An altar of grey stone, a drowned bell, a faint smell of lilies.

c7_r1b_r0.title: The Fungus Garden
c7_r1b_r0.text: A basketful of good caps, enough for a week of stew.

c7_r1b_r1.title: The Fungus Garden
c7_r1b_r1.text: You are mostly right. Roland spends a night being sick.

c7_r1b_r2.title: The Fungus Garden
c7_r1b_r2.text: The caps nod gently in the draught as you walk away.

c7_r1b.title: The Fungus Garden
c7_r1b.text: A cavern of pale mushrooms, tended once and never harvested. Some are edible. Some are not.

choices.text: Leave it. Fungus is not food.

c7_r1c_r0.title: The Drowned Armoury
c7_r1c_r0.text: A mail-shirt, two good axes, a helm. You are better armed.

c7_r1c_r1.title: The Drowned Armoury
c7_r1c_r1.text: A dwarf's ghost nods, from somewhere you cannot see.

c7_r1c.title: The Drowned Armoury
c7_r1c.text: Racks of dwarf-steel, half-submerged, rusting in the dark.

choices.text: Leave it. The dead may need it more.

c7_r2a_r0.title: The Counting-House
c7_r2a_r0.text: Every coin in the hoard is recorded, and beside each entry, a name. The god tracks what it owns. Take the ledger and you could unmake the hoard.

c7_r2a_r1.title: The Counting-House
c7_r2a_r1.text: The ledger burns green. Somewhere above you, a coin rings.

c7_r2a.title: The Counting-House
c7_r2a.text: A tiny office, desks and abacuses and a book of accounts the size of a door. Whoever kept the ledger kept it faithfully until the end.

choices.text: Burn it. The numbers should not exist.

c7_r2b_r0.title: The Mimic Vault
c7_r2b_r0.text: The chest bites the spear in half. You step back, smiling, as it settles.

c7_r2b_r1.title: The Mimic Vault
c7_r2b_r1.text: It bites. The coin is real. You are missing a fingertip.

c7_r2b.title: The Mimic Vault
c7_r2b.text: A small chamber. A chest, open, gold glittering. Too obvious.

c7_r2c_r1.title: The Idol Gallery
c7_r2c_r1.text: Its face is not a face. It is a hundred faces folded together. You see it in your dreams for weeks.

c7_r2c_r2.title: The Idol Gallery
c7_r2c_r2.text: A ruby the size of an egg. It is warm. It is humming.

c7_r2c.title: The Idol Gallery
c7_r2c.text: A hundred golden idols in a hundred poses of reverence. Each wears the face of the thing below.

choices.text: Pry out a gem. A king's pocket is never full.

c7_r3a_r0.title: The Sergeant's Room
c7_r3a_r0.text: He recorded the lich's coming, and the six levels, and a back-way around the Market: a ladder behind the third pillar.

c7_r3a_r1.title: The Sergeant's Room
c7_r3a_r1.text: A small kindness. A small dignity. Hetta sings something under her breath.

c7_r3a.title: The Sergeant's Room
c7_r3a.text: A small room with a bunk, a table, a dead dwarf slumped in a chair. A journal open before him.

c7_r3b_r0.title: The Chained Pit
c7_r3b_r0.text: They are weak, but they are alive. Seven more mouths for the road, and seven more reasons to win.

c7_r3b_r1.title: The Chained Pit
c7_r3b_r1.text: They stumble toward the light. You hope.

c7_r3b_r2.title: The Chained Pit
c7_r3b_r2.text: Their eyes follow you out. You do not look back.

c7_r3b.title: The Chained Pit
c7_r3b.text: A pit where the lich kept the living. Seven men, shackled, filthy, barely alive.

choices.text: Free them, and send them up with Hetta.
Leave them. There is not time.

c7_r3c_r0.title: The Bunk Cellar
c7_r3c_r0.text: You have not eaten this well since Aldermont.

c7_r3c.title: The Bunk Cellar
c7_r3c.text: A cellar of crates and sacks beneath the barracks. Dry. Dry! Whole sacks of hard bread.

c7_r4a_r0.title: The Bone Library
c7_r4a_r0.text: It is a grammar of the god's language. You can read it, somehow. It reads you back.

c7_r4a_r1.title: The Bone Library
c7_r4a_r1.text: A slim volume on the binding of spirits: how to weaken a thing held by its own hoard.

c7_r4a_r2.title: The Bone Library
c7_r4a_r2.text: The books scream as they burn. It is the worst sound you have heard.

c7_r4a.title: The Bone Library
c7_r4a.text: Shelves of books bound in grey skin. A scholar's reading room, lit by green fire.

choices.text: Read the first book on the first shelf.
Look for a book on binding.

c7_r4b_r0.title: The Puppet Theatre
c7_r4b_r0.text: The little bones fall in a heap. Roland says a quiet prayer.

c7_r4b_r1.title: The Puppet Theatre
c7_r4b_r1.text: The skeleton acts out the Ford. It is accurate. It is horrible.

c7_r4b.title: The Puppet Theatre
c7_r4b.text: A stage. A velvet curtain. Behind it, the skeleton of a child with strings attached.

c7_r4c_r0.title: The Pawn-Shop
c7_r4c_r0.text: A small tin charm, warm as a bird. It will turn aside one blow.

c7_r4c_r1.title: The Pawn-Shop
c7_r4c_r1.text: Drink it and the dead's stare cannot freeze you.

c7_r4c.title: The Pawn-Shop
c7_r4c.text: A shop with a dozen grey stalls. A pale clerk behind the counter does not look at you, but speaks.

choices.text: Sell a pipe-leaf for a charm of warding. (1 pipe)
Buy a vial of stillwater. (50 coin)

c7_r5a_r0.title: The Weeping Vault
c7_r5a_r0.text: Your sleeves are ruined. Your skin, mostly, is not.

c7_r5a_r1.title: The Weeping Vault
c7_r5a_r1.text: A vial of acid, perhaps useful against the god's hoard.

c7_r5a.title: The Weeping Vault
c7_r5a.text: A vault where the stone itself weeps. The drops, if you catch them, burn like acid.

choices.text: Collect the weeping in a flask.

c7_r5b_r0.title: The Echo Chamber
c7_r5b_r0.text: "Gregory," it says. "Come down. Come down and rest." You step back, shaking, with the voice still in your ear.

c7_r5b_r1.title: The Echo Chamber
c7_r5b_r1.text: The echoes fall silent. The fourth voice does not return.

c7_r5b.title: The Echo Chamber
c7_r5b.text: A circular room that returns every sound three times. Your footsteps. Your breath. A fourth voice, quieter, speaking your name.

c7_r5c_r0.title: The Drowned Reliquary
c7_r5c_r0.text: A finger-bone of the saint. Anselm weeps. The Skull stirs in its box, as if greeted by a brother.

c7_r5c_r1.title: The Drowned Reliquary
c7_r5c_r1.text: Some things are not for the taking.

c7_r5c.title: The Drowned Reliquary
c7_r5c.text: In a pool of black water, a casket of silver. A relic, half-submerged. You know the sign on the lid: Saint Gregory's own.

choices.text: Retrieve it, whatever the water does.
Pray over the casket and leave it.

c7_camp1_roland.title: By the Fire: Roland

c7_camp1_anselm.title: By the Fire: Anselm
c7_camp1_anselm.text:
Anselm has not slept since the Ford. He tells you, softly, that the Skull is lighter some days than others, and that on the heavy days he can feel it watching.

"I have wondered whether I am keeping it," he says, "or whether it is keeping me."

c7_camp1_durgan.title: By the Fire: Durgan

c7_camp1_theodore.title: By the Fire: Theodore
c7_camp1_theodore.text:
Sir Theodore does not sleep. He sits upright in the dark, and speaks only when addressed.

"I remember dying," he says. "I remember the Ford, and then a very long quiet, and then your voice. I do not remember being afraid. Is that wrong?"

c7_camp1_hetta.title: By the Fire: Hetta
c7_camp1_hetta.text:
Hetta spreads her cloak and tells you she has never trusted a king. Her father was a smith who refused to kneel to one. She says it with a grin.

"But you are a funny sort of king," she says. "You listen."

c7_camp1.title: A Camp in the Dark
c7_camp1.text:
You find a niche in the stone that is dry enough, and a corner that is quiet enough, and you make a small fire of dwarf-coal.

The mountain presses on all sides. Somewhere above, the world is burning. But for an hour, here, there is a fire and a few people who trust you.

c7_final_skull_try.title: A Dimmed Relic
c7_final_skull_try.text:
Anselm lifts the Skull. It is not what it was. The light is smaller. The silence is shorter.

The god's four hundred eyes turn toward it, and it laughs, and the laugh is the sound of coins pouring.

"Smaller," it says. "Fainter. You spent some of it on a child."

choices.text: Add your will to Anselm's. Bear the weight with him.
Hold. The relic shard in your pocket may be enough.

c7_final_skull_cost.title: The Cost
c7_final_skull_cost.text:
The Skull holds. Anselm does not. He sinks to his knees, blood from his nose, hands white around the relic, and still holds it up.

The god comes apart, slowly, and Anselm does not rise again for a month.

c7_final_blade.title: The Rune-Blade
c7_final_blade.text:
You see it now: the seam in the throne where coin met bone. Durgan's rune on the blade begins to glow, a low red like banked coals.

"The heart," Malgareth said. The ledger said the heart. You step inside the god's reach, and drive the blade in.

c7_final_bell.title: Far Above, A Bell
c7_final_bell.text:
You hold. Roland holds. Theodore holds the door. The god's hundred arms beat on you like a storm.

And then, from very far above — a hundred feet of stone and six sealed levels — a sound. A single note, rolling down through the mountain like a thrown cloth. The Bell of Saint Gregory, with the Skull in its heart, ringing for the king.

The god *stops*. Coin by coin, bone by bone, it comes apart.

c7_final_horn.title: The Horn of Durgan
c7_final_horn.text:
Durgan lifts the great horn and blows a note that rattles the gold on the walls. From the stair behind you comes an answering roar, hundreds of voices, hammers on shields.

Bruni's dwarves pour into the throne-room like a flood of iron. The god turns to face them. It is the moment you have been waiting for.

c7_final_horn_hit.title: A Coalition of Stone
c7_final_horn_hit.text: Dwarf and man and the undying knight strike together. The god cannot hold both fronts. Coin falls like rain.

c7_final_malgareth.title: The Steward Turns
c7_final_malgareth.text:
A step on the stair. Another. A cloaked figure in grey stops at the doorway of the throne-room, and lifts his hood.

"I am tired of following," says Malgareth, and for the first time in three hundred years, he sounds young.

He raises his hand. The green light flares. The god turns to look at its steward, and for a moment, it is afraid.

c7_final_name.title: The God Calls You By Name
c7_final_name.text:
"Gregory," it says, in the voice you heard in the Echo Chamber, in the ledger, in the coin. "You have carried a small hoard of your own. A crown, a Court, a kingdom's worth of guilt. I see it. I know its weight."

You are not sure whether it is lying.

"Take mine. All of it. The Deepholt's treasure. The six levels. A thousand years of servants who never tire. And in return — only that you *keep* it."

choices.text: Refuse. You are a king, not a hoarder.

c8_victory_hub.title: The Quiet

choices.text: Carry the Skull back up. The war is over.
Install the Skull in a shrine at the Bell. Found the new Order of Saint Gregory.
Free Malgareth. He has earned an end.
Bind yourself with the Skull, as Theodore was bound. Be the mountain's undying king.
Stay below. Keep the Skull here, with the thing that cannot be allowed to rise again.

c8_peace.title: The Peace
c8_peace.text:
You climb for two days. At the top of the stair the sun is a white wound in the sky, and the dead lie on the slope like fallen wheat. Aldric is on the wall, and he sees the standard, and begins to weep.

The horde does not rise.

A kingdom has to decide what it is for. The war is done. What now?

choices.text: March on the Ford with the levy. Reclaim the realm.
Raise your heir to a throne that will outlast you.
Throw the greatest feast the mountain has ever seen.
Sit by the fire in the Great Hall and let the world be small.

end_return.title: The Return to the Ford
end_return.ending: RECLAMATION — The Return to the Ford

end_dynasty.title: The Dynasty
end_dynasty.text:
{{heir_healed|Your son grows into a tall, thin, watchful boy, with his mother's green eyes and your stubborn chin.}}{{heir_slow|Your son, the quiet one, grows with the patience of an oak.}}{{heir_emmet|Emmet grows into a king's heir with a wooden horse still tucked in his saddlebag.}}{{heir_tom|Tom takes the standard when you cannot carry it, one-legged and straight-backed.}}{{heir_aldric|Aldric takes the throne at twenty-one, and holds the mountain for fifty years.}}

You live to see his coronation. You live to see the crown on his head, in the Great Hall, among the dwarves and the monks and the fen-folk, and you whisper to Roland, who is very old now, that you were right to run.

Roland grunts. "You were right to stop running."

The House of Gregory outlasts the Fall.
end_dynasty.ending: DYNASTY — A Line That Outlasts the Fall

end_feast.title: The Last Feast
end_feast.text:
It is the greatest feast the mountain has ever seen. Three hundred monks drunk on dwarf ale. Dwarves dancing with widows. A bard from the Fenmarch with a drum and an eel.

At midnight you climb onto a table and make a speech nobody remembers. You wake at noon on the floor of the Chapel with Roland's cloak over you and Ambrose, laughing, holding a cup of water.

"A king should not drink so much," says the Abbot.

"A king," you say, "should have lived to need to."

{{isobel_durgan|Durgan and Isobel dance a slow, ridiculous waltz.}}{{queen_saoirse|Saoirse sits at your side and refuses to let you stand.}}

end_vigil.title: The Vigil of Saint Gregory
end_vigil.text:
The Skull is set in the Bell, and the Bell is housed in a great round tower on the mountain's shoulder. Anselm and Ambrose found a new Order: the Vigil of Saint Gregory, whose sole purpose is to keep the dead lying down.

You do not rule them. You are their first pilgrim.

For a hundred years the Bell rings at dawn, and every dawn the dead lie still, and every dawn a monk in grey wool climbs the tower stair and says the saint's name aloud.

{{saint_favour|It is said that the saint himself smiled, the first morning, and that his smile was warm.}}
end_vigil.ending: VIGIL — The Order of Saint Gregory

end_malgareth.title: A Lich Released
end_malgareth.text:
You speak the name Ambrose wrote. Malgareth hears it, and for the first time in three hundred years he looks like a man. His hands tremble. The green light drains from his eyes.

"Thank you," he says. "I have been tired for so long."

He turns to dust on the stair. He leaves behind a small, plain stool, and a ring of keys. The ring opens the sealed archive of the Deepholt, and in it, a great deal of knowledge the dwarves had lost.

{{bors_taken|You find in the archive the last letter Bors wrote, in his own hand. It is a very good letter.}}

Some things, you think, are not victories. They are mercies.

end_undying.title: The Undying King
end_undying.text:
Anselm raises the Skull and speaks the rite. It is like Theodore's, but not the same; you feel the breath leave your body, and then return, strange.

You do not age. You do not sleep. You do not tire. You sit on a plain stool in the Great Hall of the Deepholt with a pipe in your mouth, and over the years you watch your friends grow old and die: Roland, Durgan, Isobel, Saoirse, the boy Tom with his one leg.

At last, you are the only one who remembers the Ford.

It is not what you wanted. It is, you suppose, what you asked for.

end_goldking.title: The Gold King
end_goldking.text:
The god takes you gently. There is no violence. Its hundred arms fold around you like a father's, and its voice is every comfort you have ever craved.

When you wake, you are on the throne. The god is not dead; it is *you*. You wear its form as easily as a coat. The hoard is yours, and the six levels, and a legion of drowned servants, patient as stone.

Roland kneels first. It is the worst thing you have ever seen.

You rule for a thousand years. They are a very long time.
end_goldking.ending: THE GOLD KING — The Hoarder Reborn

end_regency.title: The Regency of Saoirse
end_regency.text:
You stay in the door while the others carry the Skull out. The god strikes you down in the third blow. The last thing you hear is Roland weeping, and the last thing you see is the standard, going up the stair.

Saoirse takes the regency. She holds it for eighteen years, with the fen-folk and the dwarves and the monks and an iron will. When your son is old enough, she hands him the crown with a small, secret smile, and says:

"Your father ran, once. And then, once, he did not."
